title: The Giraffe's Whisper
text: Why did the giraffe whisper so slowly? She said her words needed extra time to reach her ears! Her zebra friend waited, nodded, and whispered back. By then, the giraffe had forgotten the question, so they both laughed.
context: An original animal joke with a clear setup and punch line.

title: The Turtle's Alarm Clock
text: Why did the turtle set an alarm for next Tuesday? He wanted plenty of time to wake up! When the bell finally rang, he stretched one foot, smiled, and said, “Five more minutes.” His nap lasted until Friday.
context: An original joke about a very sleepy turtle.

title: The Goat's Report Card
text: A goat carried his report card to lunch. “Do not eat that,” said his teacher. The goat looked surprised. “Eat it? I was only reading the menu!” He took one tiny nibble, then asked for a side of crayons.
context: An original school joke featuring a hungry goat.
vocabulary: report card: a school record of learning

title: The Penguin's Sandwich
text: What did the penguin put in his sandwich? Iceberg lettuce, of course! He packed it for lunch, but the sandwich slid away across the ice. The penguin chased it and called, “Come back, you slippery snack!”
context: An original lunch joke about a penguin.
vocabulary: iceberg lettuce: a round, crisp kind of lettuce

title: The Owl Does Math
text: The owl finished every math problem at night. “Why not work during the day?” asked the fox. The owl blinked and said, “Because my answers are always brighter after dark!” The fox checked the page. One answer was a drawing of cheese.
context: An original joke about an owl's unusual homework.

title: The Snail's Fast Shoes
text: A snail bought bright red running shoes. “Will those make you fast?” asked the rabbit. “No,” said the snail, “but I will look speedy while I cross this leaf.” Three days later, the shoes were still perfectly clean.
context: An original joke about speed and style.

title: The Bear at the Library
text: A bear walked into the library and asked for a book about honey. The librarian found a big one. “Is this sweet enough?” she asked. The bear opened it, sniffed a page, and said, “It needs more pictures of bees.”
context: An original library joke about a bear.
vocabulary: librarian: a person who works in a library

title: The Frog's Raincoat
text: Why did the frog wear a raincoat in the pond? He did not want his new shirt to get wet! A fish looked at the frog's dripping sleeves and giggled. The frog said, “Fashion is harder than it looks.”
context: An original pond joke about a dressed-up frog.

title: The Mouse Turns Up the Music
text: A mouse played music from a very tiny speaker. “Can you turn it up?” asked the elephant. The mouse pushed one button. A huge squeak filled the room. The elephant covered his ears and said, “That is up enough!”
context: An original joke about a surprisingly loud mouse.
vocabulary: speaker: a device that plays sound

title: The Zebra's Pajamas
text: The zebra wore striped pajamas to a sleepover. “How can we tell when you are ready for bed?” asked the lion. The zebra smiled. “Easy! My bedtime stripes run sideways.” Everyone checked. The stripes did not, but the joke worked.
context: An original bedtime joke about a zebra.
vocabulary: sideways: from one side toward the other

title: The Dinosaur's Homework
text: Why did the dinosaur bring a ladder to school? His homework was over his head! The teacher pointed to a small worksheet and asked, “Is that really why?” The dinosaur nodded. He was very tall, and the paper was sitting on a high shelf.
context: An original school joke about a tall student.

title: The Kangaroo's Backpack
text: A kangaroo brought an empty backpack to class. “Where are your books?” asked the teacher. The kangaroo patted her pouch and said, “My backpack is only for snacks.” At lunch, she opened it. Inside was one sandwich and a very surprised toy frog.
context: An original joke about a kangaroo's unusual school bag.
vocabulary: pouch: a pocket on a kangaroo's body

title: The Chicken at the Keyboard
text: Why did the chicken sit at the computer? She wanted to peck out an email! She tapped every key with care, then pressed Send. Her message said, “Dear Farmer, please put more corn by the coop.” The farmer replied with three rows of question marks.
context: An original joke about a chicken writing email.
vocabulary: coop: a small building where chickens live

title: The Cat Goes to Space
text: What did the cat astronaut pack for the Moon? A bowl, a blanket, and a mouse map! “Why the map?” asked Mission Control. The cat purred and said, “I heard the Moon has giant craters. A mouse could hide anywhere up there.”
context: An original space joke featuring a prepared cat.
vocabulary: crater: a bowl-shaped hole in the ground

title: The Duck's Library Card
text: A duck waddled into the library and asked for a card. “Can you write your name?” asked the librarian. The duck dipped one foot in ink and stamped the page. “Close enough,” said the librarian. The new card was filed under W for Webbed Foot.
context: An original joke about a duck joining the library.
vocabulary: filed: placed in an organized group
